sources.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after alleged affairs
sources.text: Move follows admission of affair with woman alleged to be Chinese spy and reported relationship with employee Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive of Nvidia after reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and a company employee. He will be replaced on an interim basis by Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, until a full-time successor is named. The statement from Nvidia’s board of directors confirming Huang’s departure did not mention the spying scandal and personal conduct revelations that have enveloped the company, instead paying tribute to Huang’s “profound” contribution to the company he co-founded. “Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the statement said. The chipmaker’s board earlier this week appointed leading law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent” investigation into the relationship with Alice Huang, who is no relation to the Nvidia boss. The firm directed Jensen Huang to continue to helm Nvidia as the investigation was ongoing. However, late on Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang had a separate extramarital affair with a company employee named Kimberly Powell. She was Nvidia’s president of healthcare and was reportedly captured on video being affectionate with Huang at a hotel during a company conference in March. The report added to the pressure on Huang as the board met late on Wednesday. Huang’s exit from the company he co-founded in 1993 removes a senior figure in Silicon Valley at a time when the AI arms race between the US and China is at an apex. Huang owns more than 870m shares, or about 3.6% of the company and is worth $145bn (£109bn), according to Bloomberg, making him the world’s 13th richest person. Unlike many of his contemporaries at other leading tech companies, Huang has dozens of direct reports, an unusual management structure that emphasises his control over the company. The entire artificial intelligence ecosphere relies on the company, which engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. It is also one of the most valuable companies on Earth, with a market cap of more than $4tn. Nvidia and Huang have both taken a financial hit as the scandal unfolds: company shares slid about 7% in pre-market trading on Thursday after the Wall Street Journal reported Nvidia’s board was readying Huang’s ouster. While Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair without directly naming the suspected spy, he denies any knowledge that Alice Huang allegedly worked for the Chinese government. The pair were seen together around the world, dining in restaurants and attending meetings, over the past few years. Alice Huang is a businesswoman and head of the Singapore-based datacentre firm Megaspeed, who US intelligence services suspect of being a Chinese asset according to multiple reports. Jensen Huang, who has been married to his wife, Lori, since 1985, admitted in an email to employees on Sunday after days of speculation about his relationship with the Megaspeed executive that he had an affair and that he would cooperate with an internal investigation. Nvidia’s board of directors put out a statement the same day that the company was launching an investigation regarding reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Donald Trump has backed Jensen Huang , saying he had done “an incredible job” and is “an honorable guy”. Big tech industry players, including Elon Musk, have also thrown their support behind Huang. However, Nvidia’s stock has tumbled with the news, and is down more than 11% in the past few days.

sources.title: Nvidia stock falls nearly 10% as CEO Jensen Huang announces resignation
sources.text: Follow CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation here. Nvidia shares plunged nearly 10% on Thursday, sending the company's value below $4 trillion in market cap after Jensen Huang announced he would immediately step down as CEO and a member of the board at the chipmaker. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO until a new leader is appointed, Nvidia said in a Thursday statement. Harvey C. Jones, former CEO of Synopsys, will become the first-ever chair of the board. On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an affair . The CEO was romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at cloud company Megaspeed , according to The Financial Times , who U.S. intelligence officials believe is a spy for China. The New York Times on Wednesday reported that Huang had another extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at Nvidia. Powell reports to Huang, according to the Times. Before Huang resigned, several Wall Street analysts told CNBC that this departure could lead the stock to fall 20%, given how critical he has been to Nvidia's success. Nvidia's stock is already down more than 20% over the last month. Bernstein on Thursday slashed its price target on Nvidia's stock by half from $400 to $200. Stacy Rasgon, a senior analyst at Bernstein, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" on Thursday that Huang's alleged affair with a direct report means it is "much tougher for the board to leave him in position." Huang was central to Nvidia's rise, having co-founded the company in 1993 and was pivotal in transforming Nvidia from a gaming hardware player to the company at the center of the artificial intelligence boom. Rasgon said it is unclear who could be the "visionary" to lead Nvidia into the future as new CEO. "Jensen is Nvidia, right? He is the visionary. The reason they're in the position that they're in today is because he made decisions 10 years ago," Rasgon said. "Who is the right person now to make the decisions for the next 10 years? I don't intuitively know who that person would be." Earlier, U.S. lawmakers had called for Huang's resignation , adding further pressure to the CEO and the company. Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at Questar Capital Partners, said Nvidia's lack of a succession plan makes the stock "uninvestable." "Nvidia doesn't have that person in place, and so it's going to be either a choice of keeping Jensen and being faced with months and months of being hauled in front of probably congressional boards and things to explain themselves and all kinds of interrogations," Reyle told CNBC's "Access Middle East." "Or they're going to have to move on from him, and that's just going to make the stock uninvestable. That doesn't make the AI trade uninvestable, but it certainly makes Nvidia uninvestable." — CNBC's Caleigh Keating contributed to this report.

sources.text: This is CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news. The company will begin the search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang and will consider both internal and external candidates, according to the release. Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted. After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy. Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. Late Wednesday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future. Jensen Huang denied allegations that he had compromised national security or Nvidia secrets after reports of the Alice Huang affair. The news sparked concerns that Nvidia knew companies based in Singapore and Malaysia had been evading U.S. export controls in accessing its technology. The board said on Tuesday that it had hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate the intelligence allegations. Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China. In May, Huang joined Trump on a trip to China, and in August, while on stage at the All-In Summit to discuss AI safety and regulation, he took a call from Trump and put him on speakerphone. "I'm with you all the way," Trump told Huang and the audience. With Democrats poised to take over both houses of Congress and promising to investigate various matters related to Nvidia, Huang's status in Washington, D.C. was poised to change dramatically even before the affairs became public. Nvidia's fortunes exploded after OpenAI released ChatGPT in late 2022, leading to soaring demand for the chipmaker's graphics processing units, or GPUs. Nvidia's stock is up about 14-fold since then, even with a recent pullback related to the Huang scandal and the broader selloff in the AI trade. Beyond its impact on Nvidia, Huang's departure has deep ramifications for the AI industry that has turned Huang into a global spokesperson and celebrity, traversing the globe in his trademark leather jacket, touting the power of the advanced chips, models and agents. Huang has seeded the market with numerous companies that buy Nvidia GPUs, building his company's influence and establishing a deep roster of customers, beyond the hyperscalers. Nvidia has used its balance sheet to backstop leases and chip sales, and has become the centerpiece of the industry, acting as technology supplier, customer, investor, financier, and partner to scores of AI companies. "He's Mr. AI. He speaks for the industry," said Jeff Christian, CEO of Christian and Timbers, an executive search firm. "He's connected financially to everybody either through partnerships, or through lending the money to buy chips." Before Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia, SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk said, in a post on X, that it would be "an honor" to hire the embattled Nvidia founder. Musk also agreed with Gavin Baker, chief investment officer of Atreides Management, who wrote in a post on X that "Nvidia's board should wait for the results of the investigation before ousting Jensen." SpaceX is one of Nvidia's largest customers, and Nvidia invested in SpaceX via an equity investment in Musk's xAI, which is now known as SpaceXSI. In August, during a SpaceX earnings call, Musk said Nvidia had the "best AI compute" and announced SpaceX would become an Nvidia-exclusive shop, using its Vera Rubin processors to build out massive data centers. Musk and SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Huang's resignation. Nvidia's stock plunged over 13% at the open. The chip giant dropped below $4 trillion in market cap, accelerating a sharp decline so far this week. The move puts Nvidia on pace for its worst day since January 2025. Nvidia's market value has plunged by $2 trillion since the chipmaker's stock peaked in early October. Shares closed at $173.73 on Wednesday, down from a closing high of $239.24 on Oct. 6. Since Friday's close, Nvidia has lost more than $740 billion in market value. Minutes before Huang's ouster, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer suggested to CNBC that the U.S. AI buildout won't be dragged down by the scandal smothering Nvidia. "Obviously, Nvidia is a structurally important company," Greer told "Squawk Box," acknowledging the AI giant's recent stock "fluctuations" in light of its CEO crisis. "The reality is the AI buildout, data centers, the next industrial revolution — that's happening," he said. sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy, affair scandals
sources.text: After reports of Huang’s two extramarital affairs with an alleged spy and an Nvidia executive, he’s out, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is in. After reports of Huang’s two extramarital affairs with an alleged spy and an Nvidia executive, he’s out, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is in. Nvidia’s board announced that Jensen Huang — its longtime co-founder, president, and CEO — has resigned after reports of two extramarital affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with an Nvidia executive who reported to Huang. Following a late Wednesday night meeting, the board accepted Huang’s letter of resignation as CEO, president, and board member, effective immediately, with current CFO Colette Kress appointed interim CEO. Kress has been with Nvidia since 2013, with previous stops at Cisco and Microsoft. Nvidia is also changing its corporate structure in Huang’s absence, appointing former Synopsys CEO Harvey C. Jones as the first board chair in its history. The statement does not include a statement from Huang, while Kress is quoted as saying: NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years. We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders. Now Nvidia says, “The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates,” and reports about who that might be have already surfaced , putting Kress, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji , Nvidia VP Ian Buck, AMD CEO (and cousin of Jensen Huang) Lisa Su, and Arm CEO Rene Haas at the top of the list. Huang had been at the helm of what’s now known as the most powerful company in AI since its founding in 1993. In the years since, it’s become the main purveyor of the chips fueling AI advancement and deployment in the US, and it has enjoyed near-unbridled power and influence — demand for Nvidia’s chips constantly outpaces supply, and AI CEOs are constantly putting in requests to buy more, sometimes to no avail. Nvidia’s investment portfolio — worth about $99 billion and spanning AI companies from frontier labs to neoclouds — has also granted it a lot of sway in the AI space. And in recent years, Huang himself has enjoyed a close relationship with President Donald Trump. Over the past week, that influence has been a double-edged sword for Huang, after news broke that he had been involved in a romantic relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider and big customer of Nvidia itself. The Megaspeed executive was also allegedly a surveillance operative passing information along to China’s Ministry of State Security. She was focused on gaining information about advanced AI chips in the US and trying to influence the technology being made available to China, The New York Times reported. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and apologized to his family and shareholders in a memo to Nvidia employees over the weekend. As The Verge wrote earlier this week , “questions are swirling around how the affair may have influenced Huang’s reported push to sell advanced chips to China — and potentially even influenced President Trump’s own decisions surrounding AI export controls.” As of Monday , analysts, venture capitalists and even Trump had expected Huang would come out the other side of the scandal with his chief executive status intact. Silicon Valley insiders, including Elon Musk, had backed him despite the news. But on Wednesday, news broke that Huang had had a second extramarital affair — this time with an executive reporting directly to him. The New York Times , citing five people who worked at Nvidia, identified the relationship as being with Nvidia’s VP of healthcare, Kimberly Powell. Soon after the news broke, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Nvidia’s board was meeting as soon as Wednesday evening in order to decide Huang’s future at the company and potentially oust him from his role.

sources.title: Jensen Huang renuncia como CEO de NVIDIA
sources.text: Bombazo en NVIDIA, que acaba de anunciar la renuncia de Jensen Huang como presidente, CEO e integrante de la junta directiva . La decisión del empresario tiene efecto inmediato y se produce tras los escándalos que salieron a la luz en las últimas semanas por sus relaciones extramatrimoniales, una con una empleada de la empresa y otra con una supuesta espía de China. Colette Kress , quien se desempeña como jefa de finanzas y vicepresidenta ejecutiva de NVIDIA, servirá como CEO interina tras la salida de Jensen Huang. El anuncio se produce apenas horas después de que un reporte de The New York Times expusiera que la junta de la empresa estaba analizando la destitución de su cofundador y jefe . El anuncio de NVIDIA no revela los motivos detrás de la renuncia de Jensen Huang como CEO y principal cara visible. No obstante, es evidente que la determinación se desprende de la consecución de escándalos que lo tuvieron como protagonista en el último tiempo. El pasado domingo, la firma anunció el inicio de una investigación interna por las afirmaciones de que Jensen Huang había mantenido un vínculo cercano con una supuesta espía china llamada Alice Huang . El empresario reconoció haberle sido infiel a su esposa, aunque puertas hacia adentro negó cualquier conocimiento sobre una operación de espionaje en su contra. El FBI también abrió una pesquisa para determinar el alcance del asunto . Ayer, en tanto, un reporte reveló que Jensen Huang también había tenido una aventura con una empleada de NVIDIA . Esto complicó todavía más al empresario, debido a que la situación habría infringido las políticas de la compañía respecto de las relaciones entre ejecutivos y subordinados. De más está decir que este panorama era imposible de imaginar hace apenas un par de semanas. Pensar en una NVIDIA sin Jensen Huang al comando era totalmente inverosímil . Después de todo, estamos hablando no solo de uno de los fundadores de la empresa, sino del responsable de convertirla en la más importante del mundo gracias a sus innovaciones en el campo del hardware avanzado para IA. Claro que los escándalos de Jensen Huang no demoraron en impactar de forma directa sobre la economía de NVIDIA. El lunes, la acción de la compañía experimentó una caída que barrió 190.000 millones de dólares de capitalización bursátil en solo un día. La bajada se pronunció en la continuidad de la semana. Hoy, el valor de la acción mostraba una caída del 11 % antes de la apertura de los mercados. A diferencia de otras renuncias, Jensen Huang no ha brindado comentarios públicos, ni tampoco se sabe si los dará con el correr de las horas . NVIDIA ha incluido una tibia referencia a su legado en el anuncio de su salida. "Las contribuciones de Jensen a NVIDIA son profundas. NVIDIA es una de las empresas tecnológicas más trascendentales del mundo. El Consejo de Administración y la firma agradecen a Jensen sus inestimables contribuciones a la compañía y al sector", indicaron desde el gigante verde. Colette Kress, la nueva CEO interina de NVIDIA, se unió a la compañía en 2013. Se trata de una veterana con una vasta experiencia en grandes tecnológicas, habiéndose desempeñado previamente en Microsoft y Cisco. Pese al nuevo cargo temporario, Kress continuará ejerciendo sus roles actuales como jefa de finanzas y vicepresidenta ejecutiva . De hecho, la compañía ha ratificado que planea presentar sus resultados financieros del último trimestre el próximo 17 de noviembre. Todavía no se sabe si Kress tiene posibilidades de asumir el rol de CEO de NVIDIA a tiempo completo. La junta de la compañía informó la puesta en marcha de un proceso para definir al reemplazante de Jensen Huang, considerando tanto a candidatos internos como a externos. Otro cambio notorio que llega con la renuncia de Jensen Huang es que la junta de NVIDIA ha nombrado un presidente por primera vez en su historia. Dicho rol ha recaído sobre Harvey C. Jones , inversor y exCEO de Synopsys, una empresa estadounidense dedicada al desarrollo de software para el diseño de circuitos integrados complejos. "La fortaleza de NVIDIA siempre ha residido en su gente. Junto con nuestro equipo directivo, me comprometo a seguir construyendo sobre la base extraordinaria que Jensen ha forjado a lo largo de los últimos 33 años. Seguiremos impulsando el trabajo que ha convertido a NVIDIA en un referente en computación acelerada e inteligencia artificial, y aprovecharemos las oportunidades que tenemos por delante. Nuestro objetivo sigue siendo servir a nuestros clientes, socios, desarrolladores y accionistas", remarcó Colette Kress tras la salida de Jensen Huang.

sources.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO
sources.text: Jensen Huang stepped down as the chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, four days after the company announced its internal investigation into an affair he had with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. “Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately,” the Nvidia board said in a statement. Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO. The board said it “will consider internal and external candidates” for a permanent replacement. The board’s investigation was announced on November 8, slightly less than two weeks after The New York Times reported that the chief executive had been the target of a Chinese intelligence operation facilitated through his relationship with Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen. The pair have been spotted in public together at least twice, in June 2024 and May 2025 . On November 11, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also allegedly had a relationship with a direct report at Nvidia. The alleged relationship with a subordinate, along with Huang’s business dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company where Alice Huang previously held a senior position, likely played a greater role in the board’s decision to oust Huang than the Chinese espionage allegations, a source familiar with the matter tells WIRED. US intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Donald Trump on Haung’s relationship with Alice last year, but the president did not act on it. On November 6, The New York Times and Financial Times reported that Alice was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, and that she had been recruited to collect information on the Nvidia executive. (The Chinese government has rejected all claims that Alice was a spy for the country. ) Huang sent a companywide email on Sunday acknowledging his affair, apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees, and pledging cooperation with the internal investigation. The executive has been married to his wife Lori Huang since 1985 , and both of the couple’s two children work at the company. On Monday, WIRED exclusively reported that last year Huang began working with a crisis PR firm in order to manage his personal communications. In October 2025, those PR consultants started to be looped in to all press inquiries involving Huang, whether those inquiries were personal or professional in nature. The timing lines up with a New York Times report that month that the US Commerce Department was investigating whether Alice’s Megaspeed was helping Chinese companies get around American export controls with the help of a vast web of subsidiaries. The investigation was reportedly halted and transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter inquired about it. Huang has been a vocal critic of these export controls, which he argues unnecessarily constrain the market for American chips, create discrete Chinese and American tech ecosystems, and spur China to build competitive chips of their own. Huang has worked to develop a relationship with Trump in order to advocate for policies that are advantageous for Nvidia, including the idea of opening its markets to China. Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 with friends Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. The trio reportedly brainstormed their vision for the company in a Denny’s diner , and aspired to bring realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For the first few decades of its existence, Nvidia was primarily known in the gaming community for creating chips powerful enough to render high-quality in-game graphics. In 2012, after a new kind of neural network known as AlexNet won a high-profile prize in computer vision, Nvidia pivoted from high-speed computer graphics to building chips that would support artificial intelligence. Huang has repeatedly said that the introduction of AlexNet, which was developed by AI engineers Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton, was a “Big Bang”-like event for computing, Because its new GPUs proved highly effective at powering AI models that require massive amounts of processing power, the value of Nvidia shares soared in 2023 and 2024, in lockstep with the broader AI boom that began sweeping through the world economy. In the summer of 2025, Nvidia became the first company in history to cross $4 trillion in value. As of September 2026, the company controlled about 90 percent of the GPU market. Much of Nvidia’s epic rise over the few decades has been attributed not just to its cutting edge chips and its software “moat,” CUDA, that keeps developers locked into those chips; but also to the fast-thinking, controlling, charismatic, and often bombastic leadership style of Huang himself. Now, that critical part of the company’s success is out.

sources.title: Jensen Huang is out as NVIDIA CEO
sources.text: He has held the position since the company's founding. On Thursday, NVIDIA's board of directors said that Huang had resigned his position as president and chief executive of the company, effective immediately. Huang also gave up his board seat. NVIDIA named Colette Kress, the company's current executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO. "Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named," NVIDIA said. "The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates." As part of the shakeup, NVIDIA also appointed its first-ever chair of the board in Harvey Jones, who previously served as CEO and executive chairman of electronic design automation company Synopsys. "Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Jones said in a statement. "She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption." Huang's departure comes days after NVIDIA's board said it would investigate Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a former tech executive accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The board said at the time it had "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised." The FBI is also investigating , according to President Donald Trump. The New York Times later reported that Huang had also had an affair with an NVIDIA executive who reported to him, and that the two were seen "being affectionate" at a hotel during a company conference this year. A bystander who reportedly recorded the interaction was offered a nondisclosure agreement by Huang's security detail, according to the report. Huang's downfall is a stunning turn for the company, which has become a linchpin for the AI industry. He has been CEO since co-founding the company in 1993. Since then, he has transformed NVIDIA from a 3D graphics company to an AI powerhouse worth more than $4 trillion. As NVIDIA's stock price has exploded in recent years Huang has become an increasingly public face of the AI boom. He often appeared at events — usually wearing his signature black leather jacket — with fellow tech CEOs like Mark Zuckerberg and Satya Nadella . At a time when high profile AI researchers are raising the alarm about superintelligence, Huang has had a much more positive view on the technology. He argued against increased regulation of the industry and has said America should not restrict China's access to US-made chips. Huang has frequently been seen with President Trump, and was one of several tech leaders to accompany him on a recent trip to China. Asked about recent revelations , the president said he believed Huang was "an honorable guy" and that he "probably has an excuse for it." In a memo to NVIDIA employees earlier this week in which he apologized for his actions, Huang wrote that leading the company was "the privilege of my life" and that he was "committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security." He added that he was "fully committed to NVIDIA" and would "work to earn back your confidence." But the CEO who once seemed untouchable won't get the chance to do so.

sources.title: Meet Colette Kress, Nvidia’s New Interim CEO
sources.text: Nvidia’s CEO and cofounder Jensen Huang is officially out , and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress is in. The chipmaker’s board of directors announced Thursday that Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, has been named interim CEO following Huang’s resignation amid a scandal over his extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman believed by US officials to be an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Harvey Jones, the newly appointed chair of Nvidia’s board, said in a statement that Kress “has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position.” He added that Kress will be supported by an “experienced leadership team” and that the board has “full confidence” in her. Kress was among the most obvious candidates to fill the void after Huang’s departure, according to multiple tech executives and industry analysts who follow Nvidia closely, given her long tenure at the company, credibility on Wall Street and across the tech industry, and, perhaps most importantly, her deep familiarity with Nvidia’s business and finances. “She’s extremely strong-willed, professional, and whip smart. She doesn’t tolerate nonsense. She can be friendly and gracious, too,” says a former Nvidia executive who spoke on the condition of anonymity. “She obviously has a keen sense for how Jensen thinks.” “Colette is the logical choice,” says Patrick Moorhead, founder and chief analyst at Moor Insights & Strategies, who has tracked the chip industry for decades. “She has credibility with investors because she answers hard questions directly.” Moorhead says Kress has operated as much more than a “numbers” CFO. “In my conversations with her, she goes deep on the product roadmap, from rack-scale systems to networking and software,” he says. Nvidia’s board said on Sunday it was launching an independent investigation into Huang’s activities following a report by The New York Times that he had an affair with a woman named Alice Huang, who US officials suspected of being a Chinese spy. WIRED reported on Monday that Huang quietly hired a crisis communications firm sometime last year to handle matters related to his personal life. By October of that year, the firm was being looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang at Nvidia, around the same time The New York Times reported that US authorities were investigating whether a company linked to Alice Huang had helped Chinese firms evade US chip export controls. While Huang has long been the public face of Nvidia, Kress has been responsible for managing the chipmaker’s relationship with Wall Street. On earnings calls, she often details Nvidia’s financial performance, customer demand, supply constraints, and other key metrics. “One of the things we don’t focus on is the stock price. We focus on our investors and how we would like to innovate,” Kress told the Israeli business newspaper Globes in 2023. Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent more than two decades in finance roles at Microsoft, Cisco, and Texas Instruments. Huang personally recruited her in 2013, when Nvidia was still best known for its gaming graphics cards, according to Globes. Huang laid out his vision for the company’s future on a whiteboard, explaining how Nvidia could become a major supplier of computing infrastructure for artificial intelligence. Other potential successors to Huang included Ian Buck, a more than 20-year Nvidia veteran who created the company’s software platform CUDA and now oversees its high-performance computing business, and Jeff Fisher, who joined Nvidia in 1994 as the head of software sales and later became senior vice president of its GeForce unit, where he led Nvidia’s strategy for bringing GPUs to market. However, Nvidia’s unusual corporate structure has long meant that dozens of executives report directly to Huang. The company lacks a traditional chief operating officer. Even executive vice presidents aren’t necessarily given direct control over budgets, sources have told WIRED. As a result, few people within the organization have the same level of understanding of the company’s financials as Kress. The former Nvidia executive who spoke to WIRED on the condition of anonymity said that while Kress is incredibly sharp and “can step into the [CEO] role immediately without needing any guidance,” Kress doesn’t have the same engineering and technical expertise that Huang brought to his role as a founding CEO. She has also shied away from being “at the center of public attention,” this person said. Given the intense scrutiny surrounding Huang lately, this leadership style might be a welcome temporary change for Nvidia.

sources.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
sources.text: Nvidia ’s Jensen Huang has resigned from the company, following accusations of the CEO having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy , and subsequent details of a second alleged affair emerging. The Board of Directors announced that the resignation is effective immediately, and that Colette Kress, who is currently Chief Financial Officer of Nvidia, will be the interim CEO. In a press statement, Nvidia said: “Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named.” The board also said that a search for a new permanent CEO has begun, and that the successor to Huang could be either an internal appointment, or an external candidate could get the job. Because of the importance of both Huang and Nvidia in the tech industry, there could be a lot of fallout from this, so we'll be keeping this story updated live as more information and and reaction to this news emerges. This whole debacle started when Huang admitted that he had formed a "close relationship" with Alice Huang, who was once an executive of Megaspeed, a Singaporean company that is a customer of Nvidia. In a message to his then-employees, Jensen Huang wrote that "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children." But this was just the start. Outside of Apple's CEOs and AI leaders, Jensen Huang was arguably the most recognisable tech CEO. In his trademark black leather jacket, he successfully made Nvidia the dominant player in consumer gaming graphics cards, before pivoting to AI chip powerhouse. This made Nvidia one of the most successful companies in the world, so the importance of this dramatic fall from grace really can't be understated. For some background about what's led to this, check out our article by Lance Ulanoff on why this is more than just a tech soap opera . sources.text: El hombre más importante para la industria de la IA en estos momentos se marcha. Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia, ha presentado su renuncia. Una decisión que llega después de cuatro días en el ojo del huracán después de que trascendiera de que mantuvo una relación extramatrimonial con una empresaria china cliente de la multinacional que, en realidad, sería una presunta agente de inteligencia de Pekín. Este final parece haberse precipitado horas después de que trascendiera un segundo affaire, en esta ocasión con una subordinada directa. La junta directiva mantuvo este miércoles un encuentro en el que se puso su despido sobre la mesa. Finalmente, no han tenido que obligar a Huang a marcharse sino que ha dedicido dimitir, tal y como ha adelantado la agencia Reuters. La polémica ha afectado y mucho al valor de la compañía, que hasta hace apenas diez dias presumía de ser la empresa con mayor capitalización bursátil del mundo, puesto que recuperó Apple el pasado 3 de noviembre. En las últimas cinco sesiones, Nvidia ha perdido cerca de 470.000 millones de dólares. Algo que ha profundizado en una caída que se inició hace un mes, cuando ha visto esfumarse 1,32 billones de su valor. En cuatro semanas ha pasado de 5,52 billones de dólares de valor en Bolsa a 4,19 billones tras el cierre de los mercados este miércoles. Y es previsible que esa caída pueda acentuarse en los próximos dias, porque su sucesión no es precisamente sencilla. Hasta que saltó el escándalo de la presunta trampa de miel tendida por una espía china (un extremo, por cierto, que Pekín niega), nadie había cuestionado públicamente el liderazgo hiperpersonalista que Jensen Huang ejecutaba sobre la organización. Durante más de 30 años, el tiempo que ha pasado desde que fundó la compañía en 1993, ha creado y mantenido una estructura en la que prácticamente todas las decisiones de negocio, fuesen el ámbito que fuesen, eran supervisads por él. Él dirigia y controlaba a un grupo de sesenta ejecutivos que le reportaban diariamente. A diferencia de otras grandes tecnológicas, concentró todo el negocio en su figura. No hubo un presidente ni un vicepresidente ejecutivo que estuviese llamado a reemplazarle. El hombre más importante para la industria de la IA en estos momentos se marcha. sources.title: China’s Nvidia Honeypot Isn’t Surprising. Jensen Huang Fell for It Anyway
sources.text: There’s a specific mantra drilled into government workers, military officers, and intelligence personnel during counterintelligence briefings: “If she’s a 10 and you’re a 5, she’s a spy!” Or, as the US Army’s Counterintelligence Command posted on Valentine’s Day: “It doesn’t take a mathematician to figure out ‘10 + 5 = honeytrap.’” The very beautiful woman who is suddenly interested in your very ordinary existence probably has ulterior motives , is the message. Jensen Huang surely doesn’t live a typical life—he’s a centibillionaire, the swashbuckling CEO of Nvidia, one of the hottest and most geopolitically consequential companies of the 21st century. Surely he’s aware of the possibility that he’d cross paths with intelligence assets. In fact, it’s hard to think of many companies in the world that would be a higher priority target for foreign intelligence agencies. All of that makes the stock-shaking news this week all the more surprising. How did Huang get embroiled in a spy scandal that mixes infidelity, international espionage, the Trump administration, and the economic behemoth of the multitrillion-dollar AI industry? The story kicked off just before Halloween, with a six-byline story in The New York Times reporting that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Starting somewhere between 2024 and 2025, Huang allegedly had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a one-time executive at a Singapore-based cloud provider known as Megaspeed. US intelligence agencies warned top US officials that they believed she was a Chinese intelligence asset. So far, Nvidia’s board, which has launched its own investigation, says it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,” but that’s far from the only concern. As one would expect, China has denied any nefarious plot centered on Jensen Huang. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson on Monday said , “The narrative about so-called Chinese spies is entirely based on groundless speculation—it’s nothing more than slander and smearing.” But according to reporting by The New York Times and the Financial Times , US intelligence officials also claim that Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was reporting to China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency. On Monday, Megaspeed said on LinkedIn that US authorities found “no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities." (There’s no indication so far that Alice Huang, a one-time Chinese state journalist, is an employee or “officer” of Chinese intelligence; she’s believed to be an “asset,” an outsider who aids an intelligence agency, sometimes for pay, sometimes not.) China, though, has elevated economic espionage to a core pillar of its economic and military development, stealing the designs for everything from US fighter jets to solar panels and commercial paint recipes . “Honeypots” or “honey traps”—positioning an alluring operative to seduce or develop a relationship with a key target—are one of intelligence’s most infamous and well-established strategies. French officials have warned specifically about Chinese honeypots since at least 2011, when intelligence reports cited a pharmaceutical researcher who was seduced and then blackmailed by a Chinese spy operation. Over the past quarter of a century, as Silicon Valley emerged as a center of political and economic power, it has become a key focus of Chinese intelligence. In one plot, a Chinese national named Fang Fang spent years trying to cozy up to Bay Area politicians , including then US Representative Eric Swalwell. (While intelligence officials at the time reportedly believed Fang to be an operative, law enforcement officials never brought any charges against her). When traveling to China, US business executives have become accustomed to leaving their regular phones and computers at home and using burner devices to prevent the installation of spyware or malware (as I did, when I traveled to China for WIRED in 2019 to report on Huawei ). In 2012, when Leon Panetta was making his first trip to China as defense secretary, he and his team were advised to bathe and shower in the dark in the event his hotel room was bugged. Last year, the threat of honeypots prompted the US government to explicitly ban personnel working in China and Hong Kong from engaging in romantic or sexual relationships with Chinese citizens. More recently, US officials joined with allies to warn about China’s increasingly sophisticated “ LinkedIn espionage ”: using the business-focused social networking site to recruit and build relationships with unwitting executives. Alice Huang’s Megaspeed, for its part, is a major Pacific region player in cloud services focused on the advanced computer chips that are the heart of Nvidia’s business. The Biden administration had sharply limited the export of cutting-edge chips globally to slow China’s development of AI, but Jensen Huang has successfully lobbied the Trump administration to loosen those restrictions. Speaking at a press conference on Monday, Donald Trump denied having prior knowledge of Alice Huang’s potential espionage. “I didn’t hear about it then, but a lot of people have heard about it, and Jensen totally denies that,” Trump said . “I asked him that question: ‘Did you have any idea that she was a spy?’ He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy.’” On Tuesday, the Times reported that Marco Rubio had briefed Trump in May, right before Jensen Huang joined the president on Air Force One for a trip to China. The veracity of Trump's claims will surely be investigated, especially in the context of the famous Watergate maxim: “What did the president know and when did he know it?” Nvidia’s CEO has been publicly linked to the Megaspeed executive since at least 2024 and Alice’s husband, Kang Weigh, has reportedly known Jensen since the 2010s. sources.title: NVIDIA podría destituir a Jensen Huang como CEO tras el escándalo con la espía china
sources.text: Jensen Huang podría perder su puesto como director ejecutivo de NVIDIA . De acuerdo con The Wall Street Journal , la junta directiva estaría preparando una reunión para decidir el futuro del fundador y CEO de la compañía. Las cosas se complicaron para Huang luego de que una investigación interna descubriera vínculos con una supuesta espía china. Según el reporte, el consejo de administración considera destituir a Huang después de que salieran a la luz dos relaciones extramaritales . Hace unos días, el CEO reconoció que había sido infiel a su esposa y pidió disculpas por traicionar la confianza de su familia y de la organización. La figura en el centro de esa polémica es Alice Huang, una ejecutiva de la compañía Megaspeed y con vínculos con el gobierno de Xi Jinping. Los primeros rumores apuntaban a que Megaspeed habría ayudado a desviar chips de IA hacia China . La compañía, con sede en Singapur, se convirtió en uno de los principales clientes de NVIDIA para la construcción de centros de datos de IA en el sudeste asiático. No obstante, las autoridades estadounidenses sospecharon que Huang ayudó a contrabandear tarjetas gráficas , por lo cual abrieron una investigación a finales de 2024. La relación entre Jensen Huang y Alice Huang comenzó en 2023 y permitió que la ejecutiva china desviara 240.000 placas gráficas H100, H200 y A100 hacia el gigante asiático. The Information reveló que Huang montó una red de empresas en China junto con su hermana y esposo, incluyendo una que le ayudó a convertirse en socio preferente de NVIDIA. Este movimiento le garantizó acceso prioritario a los chips y al CEO de la empresa. Hace unas semanas surgió un reporte de que Alice Huang estaba vinculada a los servicios de inteligencia chinos. El Departamento de Justicia abrió múltiples investigaciones relacionadas con ella y el mundo se le vino encima al jefe de NVIDIA. Según informó el New York Times , Alice Huang (también conocida como Huang Le) trabajaba para el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China mientras mantenía una relación romántica con el directivo de la empresa de tarjetas gráficas. Los investigadores temen que pueda haber accedido a detalles técnicos sobre el hardware de IA de NVIDIA y las discusiones internas con la Casa Blanca. Hasta ahora, las autoridades se han centrado en su papel como ejecutiva de Megaspeed, donde aprovechó su cercanía con Jensen Huang para ayudar a eludir los controles de exportación estadounidenses. Además de esta relación, el New York Times señaló que el jefe de NVIDIA mantuvo un romance con otra empleada de la compañía . Kimberly Powell, vicepresidente del área de atención médica de NVIDIA, fue captada en un vídeo con Jensen Huang mientras se encontraban en un hotel de San José, California. Las políticas internas de la compañía prohíben este tipo de acciones, sobre todo cuando se trata de una relación extramarital entre un jefe y su subordinada. Hasta el momento de esta publicación, el futuro de Jensen Huang permanece en el aire . Si la junta decide apartarlo del cargo, NVIDIA perdería al hombre que transformó la compañía y la convirtió en una de las más valiosas del mundo. Huang ha sido el rostro visible de la empresa por más de tres décadas, primero en su etapa gamer y ahora en el desarrollo de chips para centros de datos, por lo que encontrar un sucesor será un trabajo complejo.

sources.title: The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it
sources.text: Nvidia’s chips are powering America’s AI boom. Of course Chinese spies are interested. Nvidia’s chips are powering America’s AI boom. Of course Chinese spies are interested. As espionage targets go, Jensen Huang is perhaps one of the least surprising on Earth. The Nvidia CEO runs one of the world’s most valuable companies, controls the in-demand technology fueling the AI boom, and is cozy with presidents, CEOs, and all manner of important people. He also wears a cool leather jacket. Which makes Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy — reportedly while her spying was known to US intelligence and even President Donald Trump — all the more shocking. The fallout goes well beyond his marriage, his reputation, or Nvidia itself. Experts tell The Verge the incident threatens to disrupt the entire US AI industry, potentially jeopardize national security, and could undermine America’s efforts to maintain its fragile technological lead over China in AI. “With those chips, the US lead could vanish in a matter of weeks or months.” Nvidia is the undisputed leader in advanced computer chips, among the AI industry’s scarcest resources. While many ingredients go into building AI models — including talent, energy, capital, and data — top-tier chips are one of the most important, and Nvidia is one of a handful of companies with the expertise to design or manufacture them at the cutting edge. That makes it a gatekeeper to hardware that has become a key bottleneck in global AI development. US companies — including Meta, Anthropic, and OpenAI — are racing to develop chips of their own, in part to reduce their dependence on Nvidia, even as they spend billions securing ever more compute. For China, the US’s main rival at the frontier of AI, that bottleneck is even tighter. To maintain its technological lead, the US has restricted the sale of the most advanced AI chips to the country in the hopes of slowing its progress in the sector, which has been impressive and is thought to trail the US by a matter of months. In response, China has made developing domestic alternatives a strategic national priority, though its leaders still lag Nvidia at the bleeding edge. At the same time, a thriving black market for restricted Nvidia chips has emerged. Experts tell The Verge that China could exploit access to Nvidia to accelerate its own development, or to impede the US development of AI. Getting its hands on more Nvidia chips is the most obvious win for Beijing, says Emily Kilcrease, a senior fellow and director of the energy, economics, and security program at the Center for a New American Security (CNAS) think tank. China has advantages in other parts of the AI race — including abundant energy and a solid ecosystem of open weight models — but without the latest Nvidia chips, it “cannot close the gap with US frontier capabilities,” Kilcrease tells The Verge . “With those chips, the US lead could vanish in a matter of weeks or months.” It is not clear how successful the alleged spying operation has been on that front. There is no public evidence indicating that Huang himself has helped direct restricted Nvidia chips toward China or that sensitive information about them was obtained from him. But companies linked to the alleged spy, Alice Huang — no relation to Jensen — have reportedly enabled at least $7 billion of Nvidia chip sales to China. Brookings fellow Kyle Chan tells The Verge that a concern for US industry could be that companies with alleged ties to China may have had priority access to Nvidia’s latest GPUs. “In a time of chip scarcity,” that would make it much harder for American companies to access them, Chan says. Huang is also a prominent critic of American restrictions on chip sales, and Nvidia spends a formidable amount lobbying in Washington. Last year, he successfully secured White House approval to start exporting Nvidia’s H200 AI GPU chips to “approved customers” in China and other countries. Crucially, Huang also has the ear of President Trump as well as other world leaders, giving him great influence over policy decisions. Hardware is not the only thing of value China could get from close access to Huang, Sunny Cheung, a fellow for China studies at the Jamestown Foundation think tank, tells The Verge . “I actually think too many people are focused on whether somebody managed to steal Nvidia’s trade secrets,” Cheung says, calling it a “very narrow way” of looking at espionage. “I would hope Jensen Huang isn’t foolish enough to hand over the blueprints for Nvidia’s next-generation chips to a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.” The Nvidia CEO’s relationships with other tech executives, senior policymakers, and Trump himself give him an unusually intimate view into how some of the most powerful people in the US are thinking and planning. Beijing could use information on how American companies are planning major infrastructure expansions, their compute requirements, or broad industry trends to inform its own investments and industrial strategy, Cheung says. Huang’s intelligence value could extend well beyond AI, too. “That information alone could be extremely valuable,” says Cheung, pointing to insights Beijing could glean into White House thinking about export controls or the private views of Silicon Valley executives on China and Taiwan. “When so much of America’s AI infrastructure depends on one company, any significant security or governance problem at Nvidia can create uncertainty across the industry.” But helping China advance is only one side of this equation. Disrupting Nvidia — as this scandal clearly has — could destabilize America’s entire AI industry. More than most companies, Nvidia is remarkably closely tied to the identity and reputation of its rockstar CEO. Huang cofounded the company more than three decades ago, and ever since then he has served as its president, chief executive, and a member of the board of directors. Despite holding

sources.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang? A highly unscientific list of possible successors
sources.text: It’s almost inconceivable that Nvidia would fire its rock star CEO. Yet here we are, on the precipice of this happening. Over at Kalshi, Jensen Huang’s odds of surviving the week are sitting at a lowly 30% . Even though he built one of the world’s most valuable — and, many would argue, dangerously powerful — companies, the tides have completely turned against him. He has confessed to an extramarital affair, but as of Wednesday afternoon it isn’t even clear whom he meant: Alice Huang, the Chinese executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for her country, or Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive who reports to him and who, five sources told The New York Times in an explosive new report, was also a paramour. Even if Huang is pushed out as CEO, the board members he has made very rich are unlikely to cut him loose entirely. Barring another shoe dropping, they could keep him on as chairman, a role Nvidia doesn’t currently have. But someone still has to run the company, and there’s no apparent succession plan, which leaves us, like everyone else, to speculate while we wait to see what happens next. While Huang’s 60 direct reports undoubtedly get a closer look, consider this our own parlor game, featuring some obvious and less obvious candidates: Lisa Su . The AMD CEO runs Nvidia’s most credible rival, as well as a distant cousin of Huang. The Information floated her name this week, but why would she leave her job for his? Her company stands to benefit from every day that Nvidia spends distracted by an investigation, congressional briefings, and all the mini dramas that are sure to follow. Her best move might be to send a nice note and keep her current corner office. Eric Schmidt. He was the pick of Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management, who we talked with earlier this week. Schmidt could “parachute in tomorrow and do a very good job,” Sonnenfeld said, and perhaps he could. He ran Google from 2001 to 2011, chaired the National Security Commission on AI from 2018 to 2021, and now runs the rocket company Relativity Space. Chips, software, government, rockets — it’s an impressive range. Then again, Schmidt would bring a lot of baggage when it comes to his own extramarital dalliances . It’s hard to see him clearing the board for that reason. Lip-Bu Tan . Intel’s CEO knows chips, and right now he might welcome a very soft landing. Last month, Intel reported third-quarter revenue up 21% to $16.5 billion, then warned its fourth-quarter results would fall short of Wall Street’s forecasts. The AI boom has caused a memory-chip shortage, pushing up PC prices and cutting PC sales. That’s hurt Intel (PC chips are a big part of its business), and its stock plunged 20% in after-hours trading on the warning, having already slid more than 30% since September. A move to a company that’s eating everyone’s lunch would be a pretty amazing escape hatch. Bret Taylor. The former Salesforce co-CEO and OpenAI board chair now runs the AI startup Sierra, and his resume includes a lot of the biggest brands in Silicon Valley. He co-created Google Maps, served as Facebook’s CTO, and chaired Twitter’s board through its sale to Elon Musk. He then took over as OpenAI’s board chair after the “Blip,” Sam Altman’s firing and fast return. When companies need an unflappable, likable adult in the room, they call Taylor. He probably knows nearly every customer Nvidia has, too. Ian Buck. If the board feels strongly about having a “builder” at the helm, they could do worse than the Nvidia VP who helped develop CUDA, the chip software that has become central to Nvidia’s dominance in AI. Analysts and former employees have floated him as a possible successor, and Kalshi traders give him a middling shot . He’s no household name, but the Stanford PhD seems more viable if Huang can can keep that chairman title and push for a successor he can work with. Someone else down the hall. Andrew Bell, Nvidia’s senior vice president of hardware engineering, arrived 25 years ago as a fresh Cornell grad and has been on an upward trajectory at the company ever since. Like Buck and dozens of other executives who are presumably being scrutinized, he reports directly to Huang. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is the insider most often named, but analysts say she isn’t necessarily a natural successor as an innovator and visionary, and Bell has the chip pedigree. The wild card? Lori Huang . Nobody has floated her, but hear us out: Jensen met his wife as lab partners at Oregon State, so she has been working with him since before Nvidia existed. After graduating, she worked at Silicon Graphics as a micro chip engineer (making more money than her husband, he has said), then scaled back to raise the couple’s family, and she now co-leads the family trusts. If the board wants continuity, they could do worse than a humbler Huang who is also a brainiac. There’s a reason they say that behind every great man is a great woman (and vice versa).
